what: Most holders named are payment processors: Shopify's "Payment Processors" ("may hold funds in your Shopify Payments Account while awaiting the information requested above", S01-SH-022, https://www.shopify.com/legal/terms-shopify-payments, Part I, B, Verification and Underwriting; evidence/product-class/runs/20261012T104936Z-s01-sources/items/119-shopify.com/text.txt line 226), Adyen N.V. as Processor (S01-SH-127, Adyen for Platforms terms 2.6; items/105-adyen.com/text.txt line 283) and Stripe in its own terms (S01-WC-109, Stripe terms 3.1; items/078-stripe.com/text.txt line 114). But on international Managed Markets orders the holder is Global-e, and the source calls it the merchant of record, not a processor: "Managed Markets features are powered by Global-e. After an international Managed Markets order is placed in your store, Shopify Payments processes the transaction and holds the money in a Global-e account. When Global-e goes across the border, they act as your merchant of record. Global-e holds the funds to remit the costs to proper authorities that are involved in the cross-border commerce transaction." (S01-SH-099, help.shopify.com/en/manual/international/managed-markets/overview.md, Flow of funds, read 2026-10-10; items/028-help.shopify.com/text.txt line 59). BigCommerce's quote names PayPal as powering the processing, not as holding (S01-BC-051; see line 62).
fix: - **Who the references name as holding the money:** payment processors (Shopify's Payment Processors and Adyen N.V. behind Shopify Payments; Stripe in its own terms), and, on Shopify's international Managed Markets orders, Global-e, which acts as the merchant of record (Evidence, B).

what: The correction gives two places, each with its date, and only the first is a licence rule: "at the internationally recognized government's area, as of 2026-02, payment services need a licence from the central bank (banks and licensed non-bank institutions); at the Houthis' area, as of 2026-02-11, banks and fintech companies issue e-money in cooperation with the Sana'a central bank, and non-bank institutions there were made eligible to obtain a licence to offer e-rial services (2020)". Its sources: YE-F129, the Aden central bank's instructions of 2022-09-13 (evidence/yemen/derived/20261010T050304Z-cited-sources/049-cby-ye.com/ocr.txt lines 172-173): "لايجوز لأي شخص في الجمهورية العمل كمقدم لخدمات الدفع و/أو مشغل /مدير لنظام الدفع بدون الحصول على ترخيص بذلك ساري المفعول صادر عن البنك المركزي بموجب هذه التعليمات."; YE-E950 (IGC, 2026-02; evidence/yemen/runs/20261010T050304Z-cited-sources/items/249-theigc.org/text.txt lines 1544-1546); YE-B072 and YE-B074 (2026-02-11; evidence/yemen/runs/20261010T061420Z-sanaa-rules-search/items/032-yemen-yba.com/raw.html lines 581 and 583); YE-E194 (Sanaa Center, 2022-03; items/154-sanaacenter.org/text.txt lines 875-877): "In March 2020, CBY-Sana’a issued a new directive that expanded the scope of the type of financial service providers eligible to obtain a license to offer e-rial services." The record's "In the first market, providing payment services needs a central bank licence" puts the government area's rule on the whole first market and drops both dates.
fix: - **In the first market:** in the internationally recognized government's area, as of February 2026, payment services need a licence from the central bank (banks and licensed non-bank institutions); in the Houthis' area, as of 11 February 2026, banks and fintech companies issue e-money in cooperation with the Sana'a central bank, and non-bank institutions there were made eligible in 2020 to obtain a licence to offer e-rial services (YA-102, as corrected).

what: The comparison holds. Salla: "عند قيام العميل بالدفع، تذهب الأموال أولاً إلى رصيد المدفوعات الإلكترونية" (S01-SA-003, help.salla.sa article تفعيل المدفوعات الإلكترونية, read 2026-09-22; evidence/product-class/runs/20261012T104936Z-s01-sources/items/021-help.salla.sa/text.txt line 729), and for the UAE "يحتفظ رصيد المدفوعات الإلكترونية بمستحقات مبيعات المتجر قبل تحويلها" (S01-SA-056, 2026-09-12; items/018-help.salla.sa/text.txt line 846). Zid: "المبالغ المتوفرة في رصيد حسابك في زد باي" (S01-ZD-034, https://help.zid.sa/deposits_zidpay/, 2026-08-06; items/052-help.zid.sa/text.txt line 207). Open: the column "a licence, or a licensed partner that holds the money for Sharrwah" is stated for every market, and no cited source gives it as such. YA-102 gives a central bank licence for payment services in the first market's government area (as of February 2026) and a licence to offer e-rial services in the Houthis' area; nothing cited says whether a licensed partner holding the money would serve in place of Sharrwah's own licence.

Shopify holds within its scopes (S01-SH-022, items/119-shopify.com/text.txt line 226; S01-SH-127, items/105-adyen.com/text.txt line 283). BigCommerce: the quote doesn't say a processor holds: "PayPal powers the payment processing behind the scenes through your linked PayPal account, but all transactions made through BigCommerce Payments flow through your new BigCommerce Payments account for simplified management." (S01-BC-051, https://www.bigcommerce.com/blog/bigcommerce-payments-announcement/, 2026-03-31; evidence/product-class/runs/20261013T003518Z-s01-a2-sources/items/006-bigcommerce.com/text.txt line 253). The variant S01-V-027 names "your new BigCommerce Payments account" as where the money is, and S01-BC-084 sets it apart from the PayPal account: "The balance in the BigCommerce control panel displays funds from your BigCommerce Payments account while your PayPal business account contains any other funds" (evidence/product-class/runs/20261013T053949Z-s01-bigcommerce-help-founder-machine/items/001-support.bigcommerce.com/text.txt line 643). The same article, in lines the pilot didn't record, says the account can be reached "by logging in to your PayPal account" (line 459) and that initial payments "are held for up to 21 days", citing PayPal's hold policy (line 463). WooCommerce: no cited source puts Stripe behind WooPayments. S01-WC-109 and S01-WC-120 are Stripe's own terms (https://stripe.com/legal/ssa-service-terms, 3.1 and 4.2; items/078-stripe.com/text.txt lines 114 and 554), and the WooPayments page of S01-V-015 (items/099-woocommerce.com/text.txt line 39) doesn't name Stripe.
fix: with the processor, as Shopify Payments' processors (its Payment Processors; Adyen N.V.) hold, and as Stripe's terms say of funds held by Stripe, within the scopes under Evidence
